description: Every cover letter is laid out to the Swiss business-letter format, the same in the editor preview, the PDF and the Word export: - an A4 page with the sender's full details at top left; - the recipient's address in a right-hand window position; - a "place, date" line and a subject without a label; - left-aligned text with Swiss closing wording; - an "Annexes" block.

userStories.title: A letter stores the sender's details and its annexes, editable in the editor
userStories.description: As a user, I want to enter my address, postcode and locality, phone, e-mail and enclosures once per letter, prefilled from my CV, so that the letter can carry the Swiss sender block, place and annexes.
acceptanceCriteria: Migration. A new forward migration `010_…` adds five nullable text columns to `cover_letters`: `sender_street`, `sender_postal_locality`, `sender_phone`, `sender_email` and `annexes`. The generated types are updated; Existing rows are unchanged, with the columns null; RLS policies are unchanged and still restrict every row to its owner.

API. `POST /api/cover-letters` and `PATCH /api/cover-letters/[id]` accept the five fields, validated with zod. Each is a nullable string with a length limit in `COVER_LETTER_FIELD_LIMITS`; e-mail is format-checked when not empty; Values over the limit are rejected with 400.
Editor fields. The editor's Signature section shows the five fields with labels in fr/en/de/it, under the existing sender name. Saving stores them; reopening the letter shows them.

Prefill. On a letter whose sender fields are all empty and that is linked to a CV: phone, e-mail and the locality come from the CV's `contact.phone`, `contact.email` and `contact.location`; they are prefilled in the editor and stored on the next save; a field the user has filled is never overwritten.
Annexes. An empty annexes field (null) prints the default list in the letter's language (FR-4). An annexes value the user cleared on purpose (empty string) prints no Annexes block.
Copies. A translated copy and a duplicate carry the five fields unchanged. A letter created from a job application gets phone, e-mail and locality from its CV, as `sender_name` is today.

FR-1: One canonical description of the Swiss letter defines the parts, their order, their wording and their positions. The preview, the PDF and the Word export render from it (`CLAUDE.md` §10). No rendering adds, drops or reorders a part.

FR-2: Positions on the A4 page (210 × 297 mm): margins: left 25 mm, right 20 mm, top 15–20 mm; sender block: at the top margin, left; recipient window zone: left edge at 110 mm from the page's left edge, top at 50 mm, at most 85 mm wide, at most 6 lines; the place-and-date line: at the left margin, below the window zone; font: 11 pt. These values follow common Swiss right-window templates. They are constants in the canonical description, so they can be adjusted in one place.

FR-3: Locality for the place line: `sender_postal_locality` with a leading four-digit postcode and the following space removed ("1003 Lausanne" → "Lausanne"). If nothing remains, the date is printed alone.

FR-4: Swiss wording per letter language: columns: language | subject | default sign-off | annexes label | default annexes; en "Application for {job}" | "Kind regards" | "Enclosures" | "CV, references, diplomas"; fr "Candidature au poste de {job}" | "Meilleures salutations" | "Annexes" | "CV, certificats de travail, diplômes"; de "Bewerbung als {job}" | "Freundliche Grüsse" | "Beilagen" | "Lebenslauf, Arbeitszeugnisse, Diplome"; it "Candidatura per la posizione di {job}" | "Distinti saluti" | "Allegati" | "CV, certificati di lavoro, diplomi". Default greetings stay as today, except Swiss German spelling. No default wording contains "ß".
FR-5: The letter's language is resolved as today (`resolveCoverLetterLanguage`). The date is formatted as today (`formatCoverLetterDate`), with the place prefixed by FR-3.
FR-6: New user-facing strings (field labels, placeholders) come from the dictionaries in fr/en/de/it, with parity kept. Letter wording stays in `COVER_LETTER_WORDING`.
FR-7: No new dependency.

Regression constraint: The editor's other sections, saving, the unsaved indicator, translation, Generate and Check, the preview window, the zoom controls, and the mobile layout (PR #121) behave as before. Only the page size used for "show all" changes: A4 instead of US Letter.
Regression constraint: The cards (title and flag), the download routes' authentication, ownership checks, size limits and file names are unchanged.
Regression constraint: Resumes and their exports are untouched. `pnpm test:parity` and `pnpm test:visual` stay at their baselines.
Regression constraint: The marketing tool's PDF (`cover-letter-pdf-layout.ts`) is unchanged.
Regression constraint: Text the user wrote is never rewritten. That covers the greeting, paragraphs, sign-off and annexes; "ß" in a user's own text stays as written.
Verification: The `CLAUDE.md` §14 baseline, plus `pnpm test:parity` and `pnpm test:visual` unchanged.

userStories.title: New letters start with the Swiss greeting and sign-off in their language *(Amendment 1)*
userStories.description: As a user creating a letter, I want its greeting and sign-off to follow the letter's language and the Swiss format, so that a French or German letter does not start with "Dear Hiring Manager," and end with "Sincerely,".
acceptanceCriteria: A letter created from the creation form stores an empty greeting and an empty sign-off. Today it stores "Dear Hiring Manager," and "Sincerely,". The same holds for `POST /api/cover-letters` when no greeting or sign-off is sent. A letter created from a job application stores an empty greeting and sign-off unless the AI generation provides them.

Such a letter prints the default greeting and the FR-4 default sign-off of its language, in the preview, the PDF and Word. For example: fr "Madame, Monsieur," / "Meilleures salutations"; de "Sehr geehrte Damen und Herren," / "Freundliche Grüsse".
The editor's greeting and sign-off fields stay editable. A value the user types or picks is stored and printed as written.
Existing letters are untouched: no migration, no rewrite of stored greetings or sign-offs.

FR-1: One canonical description of the Swiss letter defines the parts, their order, their wording and their positions. The preview, the PDF and the Word export render from it (`CLAUDE.md` §10). No rendering adds, drops or reorders a part.

FR-2: Positions on the A4 page (210 × 297 mm): margins: left 25 mm, right 20 mm, top 15–20 mm; sender block: at the top margin, left; recipient window zone: left edge at 110 mm from the page's left edge, top at 50 mm, at most 85 mm wide, at most 6 lines; the place-and-date line: at the left margin, below the window zone; font: 11 pt. These values follow common Swiss right-window templates. They are constants in the canonical description, so they can be adjusted in one place.

FR-3: Locality for the place line: `sender_postal_locality` with a leading four-digit postcode and the following space removed ("1003 Lausanne" → "Lausanne"). If nothing remains, the date is printed alone.

FR-4: Swiss wording per letter language: columns: language | subject | default sign-off | annexes label | default annexes; en "Application for {job}" | "Kind regards" | "Enclosures" | "CV, references, diplomas"; fr "Candidature au poste de {job}" | "Meilleures salutations" | "Annexes" | "CV, certificats de travail, diplômes"; de "Bewerbung als {job}" | "Freundliche Grüsse" | "Beilagen" | "Lebenslauf, Arbeitszeugnisse, Diplome"; it "Candidatura per la posizione di {job}" | "Distinti saluti" | "Allegati" | "CV, certificati di lavoro, diplomi". Default greetings stay as today, except Swiss German spelling. No default wording contains "ß".
